title: Lower Fraser 2021 — Sentinel-1 candidate inundation v2
location: Sumas Prairie / Lower Fraser Valley, British Columbia
summary: Sentinel-1B observations show event-period VV backscatter change in the Lower Fraser Valley. A predeclared darkening/low-backscatter rule identifies candidate open-water inundation on eligible low-slope, known-baseline land. This is an exploratory indicator, not independently validated flood extent or damage.

temporal.description: Actual catalogue acquisition dates: 2021-10-15, 2021-10-27, 2021-11-08. 3 matched source frames. Search window 2021-10-15 to 2021-11-13 (exclusive end). Same-track VV temporal composite after linear-power spatial smoothing; the comparison is the 20 November acquisition, not a simultaneous peak-event inventory.

methods.title: Direct, matched radar observations
methods.description: Sentinel-1B ascending relative orbit 64: 15/27 October and 8 November baseline, 20 November 2021 comparison. Select the track using shared coverage only; median same-track VV after 30 m-radius linear-power smoothing. Exact scene IDs and all evaluated tracks remain in frozen source_selection.json.

methods.title: Explicit baseline and indicator
methods.description: Require documented WorldCover 2020 known categories, shared SAR and slope <5°. Exclude any contributing WorldCover class-80 water plus observed JRC 2020 permanent water. On eligible cells, VV ≤−16 dB and decrease ≥3 dB defines an exploratory candidate. Nine threshold combinations are reported; none was chosen to optimize reference agreement.

methods.title: Uncertainty and display
methods.description: SAR geometry, smoothing, wet soil, land management and vegetation confound water interpretation. Source comparison is one event-period acquisition. Display backscatter saturates outside −25–0 dB; differences saturate outside ±8 dB; numerical TIFFs retain full values. No independent field accuracy score is available.

methods.title: Frozen export and independent audit
methods.description: Original Colab selection, numerical manifest, processing receipt and provider audit remain byte-identical with unapproved history. Independent local checks rerun full numerical TIFFs. The portable source package retains those inputs; the website ships durable PNGs and hashed records. No credentials or live Earth Engine tile URLs are used.

limitations: Exploratory satellite observations, not independently validated damage, an official affected-area total or an emergency warning. Blank/excluded pixels are unknown, not unchanged.

Shared SAR observations and independently known WorldCover baseline cover 100.00% of this fixed box; candidate evaluation covers only 48.44% after slope and permanent-water exclusions. Those exclusions are not confirmed dry land.

Candidate area varies from 1621.7 to 4092.6 ha across nine predeclared threshold combinations; that sensitivity is not a confidence interval. Smooth fields, wet soil and management can mimic water; urban/vegetation-covered flooding may be missed.
Six comparison pixels exceed the exploratory +20 dB range screen (maximum 21.94 dB). Values were retained, and none is a candidate; the screen is not a universal physical ceiling.
Exploratory candidate open-water inundation, not independently validated flood extent, water depth, damage, exposure, or an emergency warning.
The −16 dB post-event and 3 dB decrease thresholds are predeclared exploratory choices, not locally calibrated universal water thresholds or an accuracy guarantee.

Same relative orbit and pass reduce viewing-geometry differences. Earth Engine GRD is terrain-corrected, but is not radiometrically terrain-flattened; a <5° slope filter is not a layover/shadow correction.

Wet bare soil, smooth fields, land management, freeze/thaw, wind, SAR noise and changing incidence geometry can mimic or hide inundation. Urban or vegetation-covered flooding can increase backscatter or remain undetected.

Temporal medians and 30 m-radius spatial smoothing suppress speckle and also erase narrow, short-lived or heterogeneous flood signals. The 20 m export grid is not a claim of 20 m independent resolving power.
The post window is an event-period composite, not a simultaneous or peak flood snapshot. The pre window may already contain wet or flooded locations; no change is not proof of no flooding.

Baseline support comes from observed, documented ESA WorldCover 2020 land-cover classes, not from filling JRC no-data as dry land. Any contributing WorldCover permanent-water class 80, plus observed JRC2020 class 3, is excluded. Both baseline products can misclassify boundaries and miss changes before the event; seasonal water remains eligible.

WorldCover class 80 is aggregated conservatively: any native permanent-water overlap excludes the full 20 m analysis cell, widening water exclusions along boundaries. WorldCover2020 is a land-cover model, not independent field truth or proof of dry conditions in November 2021.
No-data, missing baseline/DEM, high slope, insufficient observations and permanent water are excluded from candidate evaluation; blank map pixels are not confirmed dry land.

The fixed bounding box covers a Lower Fraser case study. Results must not be extrapolated to the whole British Columbia event. No SAR coherence or earthquake/tornado damage inference is performed by this module.
